💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars.
  • That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the company was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.
  • Sources indicate that according to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that volkswagen’s revived Scout brand finally has vehicles coming off the line in South Carolina, but they’re validation units, not customer cars. Scout confirms the first deliveries of the Traveler SUV and Terra pickup won’t happen until 2028.

That’s two years later than the 2026 production start the company was talking about before it even broke ground on its $2 billion factory.

Sources indicate that according to Scout’s announcement dated November 12, construction at the Production Center north of Columbia is in its final phase and most of the manufacturing equipment is installed. The Body Shop, Paint Shop, and Assembly Shop are all being used for the first validation builds.

Sources indicate that the Body Shop is the most automated part of the plant. Scout indicates more than 750 robots join roughly 160 parts into each body, laying down about 5,000 weld points per vehicle, with AI-supported weld monitoring and a metrology system checking the results. At full capacity, the shop is designed to handle about 40 vehicles per hour.

Bodies then go through an electrified paint shop before landing in final assembly, where they’re married to the chassis and get their wiring, glass, seats, and wheels.

CEO Scott Keogh is clearly happy to have something physical to point to, saying that “what we are building in Blythewood is no longer a promise on paper.”.

Industry observers note that scout also shared photos of a Terra pickup and a Traveler parked inside the plant. Its own fine print notes that they show “concept and validation vehicles” with optional features, so don’t read too much into what’s on display:.

Recent findings suggest that fair enough. But Scout is also careful about what this stage is. Teams are confirming the equipment is installed and works, and checking engineering, buildability, and parts maturity. Process validation and scaling up to production speed come later. Validation builds will continue “into 2027,” followed by pre-production builds, and then customer deliveries in 2028.

The firm says the plant will create more than 4,000 jobs, and it’s spending another $300 million on an onsite supplier park expected to support about 1,000 supplier jobs.

Industry observers note that when Keogh laid out the plan in late 2023, Scout mentioned it would start production in 2026 with deliveries shortly after. That was still the target when Scout broke ground in Blythewood in February 2024.

By the Traveler and Terra unveiling in October 2024, production had moved to 2027. Keogh then said in March that he expects the first customer to get a vehicle “sometime in 2028,” and that’s now the official line in Scout’s own press materials.

Industry observers note that it might not even be the end of it. Industry forecaster AutoForecast Solutions has the Traveler starting production in September 2028 and the Terra in March 2030. Scout hasn’t confirmed those dates, but it hasn’t given more precise ones either.

The product itself has also changed under the hood. Scout launched as a pure EV brand, then added the “Harvester” range-extender option at the reveal. According to Keogh, Scout has more than 160,000 reservations, and 87% of them are for the gas-generator version. Those are $100 refundable reservations, not orders.

Der Spiegel reported earlier this year that integrating the range extender, which wasn’t part of the original plan, was among the technical problems pushing the timeline back.

For comparison, Tesla unveiled the Cybertruck in November 2019 and delivered the first ones four years later, a delay that was widely mocked. Scout is now on a similar four-year path from reveal to customer, and that’s for the SUV it’s launching first.

According to recent reports, A working body shop with 750 robots isn’t vaporware. Scout has a real factory, a real workforce, and two vehicles that people clearly want. 160,000 reservations is a major number for a brand that hasn’t sold a single vehicle in 46 years.

But validation builds are an early step, not a finish line. Scout still has to go through pre-production, prove its processes, and ramp to rate, and every one of those stages is where latest automakers usually lose time. Rivian and Lucid both learned that the hard way.

Recent findings suggest that september 28? So we're 23 months away? I'm surprised the validation build yadda yadda stuff is supposed to take so long. It's not like VW doesn't know how to do this stuff, and that's a lot of money and equipment to sit mostly idle while 180,000 reservations holders are waiting for their cars. Maybe they're waiting for the market to change or are considering a whole other brand or product line?

In a recent development, and the market Scout was designed for in 2022 no longer exists. The EV tax credit is gone, and most of Scout’s own reservation holders picked the gas generator. In the US, the range-extender market is still early, unlike in China, where they are already popular.

But by 2028, Ford, Ram, and Jeep all initiative to have range-extended trucks and SUVs on sale. Scout’s main advantage was being early with a cool, rugged, American-built electric truck. That advantage shrinks every quarter.

We’re still rooting for these vehicles. The Traveler and Terra are among the best-looking designs in the segment. But a $100 reservation is easy to walk away from, and the question is how many of those 160,000 people are still waiting in 2028.

Sponsored by Eli Lilly and Company.

One of the body’s most vital organs—the brain—can be overlooked, even though it guides nearly everything we do.

It has been revealed that at its core, brain health is about how well your body’s command center functions—processing emotions, coordinating movement, and interpreting what you see, hear, taste, touch, and smell. It also includes cognitive health—your ability to think, learn, and remember.

According to recent reports, because the brain plays such a central role in everyday life, you don’t have to wait until something feels off to start taking care of it. Brain changes associated with Alzheimer’s disease can begin about 20 years before symptoms appear, making a proactive approach to brain health an important part of caring for your overall health.

Recent findings suggest that this messaging inspired actress, author, and advocate Julianne Moore to partner with Eli Lilly and Tech giant on their Brain Health Matters campaign to encourage people to prioritize their brain health. “From my conversations with people living with Alzheimer’s disease, I’ve seen how much proactive care matters,” Moore says. “That’s why I’m helping to encourage everyone to prioritize their brain health through regular conversations with their doctors.”.

In a recent development, not sure where to begin? Here are five ways to make brain health a priority part in your overall health.

You might not have any concerns about cognitive decline, much less dementia. But taking a proactive approach to cognitive health doesn’t have to wait until later in life—or until something feels off. One brain change associated with Alzheimer’s disease involves amyloid, a protein the body produces naturally. Talking to your doctor can help you understand your personal risk factors and discuss whether steps such as establishing a cognitive baseline and adopting brain-healthy habits may be appropriate for you.

In a recent development, add brain health to your “must-ask” list for medical appointments and come prepared with specific questions to guide the conversation. Ask your doctor whether a cognitive assessment is appropriate for you. This spoken, written, or digital evaluation can provide a starting point for monitoring your memory and thinking over time.

While a cognitive assessment cannot diagnose a condition on its own, establishing a baseline and completing follow-up assessments as recommended by your doctor may help spot early signs of memory and thinking concerns and monitor changes over time.

Here’s what you may want to ask your doctor:.

Research highlights that up to 45 percent of dementia cases, including those caused by Alzheimer’s disease, may be prevented or delayed by managing changeable risk factors. These include blood pressure, cholesterol, and diabetes; lifestyle habits around diet, exercise, alcohol consumption, and smoking; and even hearing loss, depression, traumatic brain injury (TBI), and sleep.

Industry observers note that you can’t change everything that affects your risk—such as age, family history, or certain genetic markers. But your doctor can help you understand the risk factors that may apply to you and build a plan to manage those that can be changed. The following brain-healthy habits can be a good place to start:.

In a recent development, once you understand your risk factors, establish a cognitive baseline, and identify brain-healthy habits that could work for you, the next step is bringing those pieces together. Work with your doctor to create a strategy based on your individual health needs.

Your plan might include ways to manage changeable risk factors, behaviors that support your brain health, and a schedule for revisiting your cognitive health with your doctor. Regular conversations with your doctor about these topics can help you take action early and help support your brain health for the future.

Honest discussions around brain health can help go a long way toward reducing stigma and helping others feel more comfortable seeking information, support, and care. Opening up—even in small ways—can make a difference, whether you’re checking in with loved ones, sharing your own concerns, or simply normalizing the topic in everyday life.

“Brain health is something we don’t talk about often enough,” Moore says. “There’s so much fear around cognitive health and even talking to a doctor about getting an assessment. I think it needs to be normalized.”.

To learn more about how you can be proactive for your brain health, visit BrainHealthMatters.com.

#189960. Coffee could have anti-aging benefits. Here’s why.

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1144 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Coffee could have anti-aging benefits. Here’s why.

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1144 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There are a handful of foods and beverages—red wine, eggs, and cooking oils—whose reputations tend to pendulum-swing routinely between “lifesaving” and “death sentence.” I usually hedge my bets by eating these confusing foods in moderation.
  • It has been revealed that the one item I have trouble consuming in moderation might be the most contentious of all: coffee.
  • Recent findings suggest that despite my unwavering devotion to coffee, the jury is still out on whether my daily fix is actually good for my health.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There are a handful of foods and beverages—red wine, eggs, and cooking oils—whose reputations tend to pendulum-swing routinely between “lifesaving” and “death sentence.” I usually hedge my bets by eating these confusing foods in moderation.

It has been revealed that the one item I have trouble consuming in moderation might be the most contentious of all: coffee. I am so hopelessly addicted to the stuff that I usually need at least one cup of coffee before going out to meet a friend for coffee.

Recent findings suggest that despite my unwavering devotion to coffee, the jury is still out on whether my daily fix is actually good for my health. Throughout my lifetime, coffee has variously been purported to protect my heart, disrupt its rhythm, reduce my risk of cancer, and increase it. All I know is it helps me become a fully conscious person every morning. But could my coffee habit actually reduce wrinkles and help me age more gracefully?

A new study conducted at Texas A&M suggests that certain compounds in coffee might protect the body against aging and inflammation.

According to recent reports, however, according to Dr. Dung Trinh, the chief medical officer at Healthy Brain Clinic in Long Beach, California, it’s probably too soon to pop open the champagne (or brew a celebratory pot) over the potential perks of your coffee habit.

“It’s far too early to treat coffee—or caffeic acid—as an anti-aging intervention,” Trinh tells Popular Science.

It has been revealed that despite its inconsistent status as a health food, coffee has been consistently linked to longer life and a lower likelihood of certain diseases, though it’s not certain why. The Texas A&M study, led by Dr. Stephen Safe, focused on a cellular receptor called NR4A1.

In a recent development, NR4A1 is a protein that regulates how cells respond to stress and damage. The study found that several compounds in coffee, particularly polyphenols—plant compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties—bind to the NR4A1 receptor. One of these polyphenols, caffeic acid, is found in coffee and many other plants and, despite its name, has nothing to do with caffeine. These compounds seem to promote NR4A1’s protective effects, including mitigating cellular damage and slowing the growth of cancer cell line in laboratory models.

According to recent reports, in other words, the harder your NR4A1 proteins are working, the better your cells may be at fending off damage. Sign me up!

Industry observers note that after researchers removed NR4A1 from cells in the lab, those benefits stopped, suggesting this receptor may help produce them. So, if coffee really helps NR4A1 do its job, we might just have a new anti-aging drink on our hands.

Interestingly, caffeine does not appear to play a key part in this mechanism, Trinh indicates. Instead, those benefits seem to come from coffee’s other compounds, like caffeic acid and its fellow polyphenols.

“What stood out to me was that the story was not really about caffeine,” he notes. “I also found it interesting that the researchers did more than simply show that these compounds could bind to the receptor—they demonstrated NR4A1-dependent effects in cells. That makes the mechanism more compelling.”.

Translation: The study didn’t just show that coffee compounds attach to NR4A1; it demonstrated that this binding actually seems to activate the protein’s protective effects.

Consistent with this, the study also found that decaf coffee demonstrated similar protective effects on the lab cells, providing further evidence that coffee’s benefits may not have anything to do with caffeine at all.

Industry observers note that “One of the interesting messages from this paper is that coffee should not be thought of as simply a delivery system for caffeine,” Trinh says. “Caffeic acid, chlorogenic acid, ferulic acid, and several other coffee compounds all interacted with NR4A1, while caffeine revealed much more variable NR4A1-related activity.”.

So, coffee’s superpower might not come from caffeine at all, at least when it comes to anti-aging benefits.

Before you start guzzling triple lattes in the name of cellular protection, know that “more” does not always mean “better.”.

In a recent development, “We simply cannot infer from this study that more coffee means more NR4A1 benefit,” Trinh indicates. This is because the researchers studied coffee extracts and purified compounds in a lab setting rather than giving human subjects increasing amounts of coffee and measuring NR4A1 activity. Plus, in human biology, it’s possible to have too much of a good thing, Trinh says.

Sources indicate that “At some point, additional coffee can bring unwanted effects from caffeine, including sleep disruption, anxiety, palpitations, or increases in blood pressure in susceptible people,” he notes. “Those effects could counteract other health benefits. So, this study should not be interpreted as establishing either an optimal number of cups or a dose-response relationship for this pathway.”.

Trinh adds that as compelling as the study’s findings are, he doesn’t yet believe they justify changing recommendations around coffee consumption.

Earlier studies have linked coffee drinking to living longer and to better outcomes for some age-related conditions, Trinh indicates. But those studies couldn’t explain why. This one offers “one possible biological explanation,” he says.

It has been revealed that like most early-stage research, Trinh says, this study can’t be applied to humans sipping their morning “cup of ambition.” Much of the work used a specific cancer cell in the lab, along with mouse immune cells, rather than testing regular human coffee drinkers directly. And while the study identified a potentially promising mechanism, it’s not clear how this mechanism will translate to human health outcomes.

Ultimately, Trinh says, no single food or compound is likely to be the deciding factor in how well we age.

For a coffee addict like myself, though, these findings are the best kind of wake-up call. Coffee may or may not turn back the clock, but it does stop me from hitting snooze 15 times.

“The much bigger determinants of healthy aging remain things such as regular physical activity, good sleep, avoiding smoking, controlling blood pressure and metabolic risk, maintaining social and cognitive engagement, and eating an overall nutritious diet,” Trinh says.

“This study is a promising piece of the scientific puzzle, not a prescription for another cup of coffee.”.

Industry News: Waymo halts highway operation nationwide after CA DMV pause

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (897 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.
  • Waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017.
  • In a recent development, the vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Waymo has pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after the California Department of Motor Vehicles ordered the company to pause highway operation in the state, following a viral video showing a Waymo trying to pass a police blockade.

Waymo is Google’s robotaxi subsidiary, which has been operating autonomously on public roads in some form since 2017. It has now expanded to 15 areas, recently adding another 250 square miles just last month.

In a recent development, the vehicles can be hailed through Waymo’s app, and operate with no driver in the driver’s seat, 24/7 in the covered areas. Since it can operate at any time but only within geofenced areas, this counts as “level 4” autonomy, as compared to the level 2 autonomy available on most consumer vehicles.

Until recently, Waymo only operated on city streets. These are more complex than highways, but lower speed. Accidents are more common on city streets than on highways, but can be more spectacular on highways given the higher speeds involved.

Most driver assist systems have been rolled out gradually, starting with highways, due to this lower complexity. But Waymo started with city streets first, bucking that trend.

According to recent reports, the company started offering rides on highways late last year, but only in limited markets. It had been testing highway operation for several years prior, typically with a driver and with no public ridership.

Everything was going pretty well, with Waymo declaring its autonomous vehicles have stopped 841 injuries over the course of their 271 million miles of operation. And in terms of competition, Waymo is far ahead of Tesla’s Robotaxi effort.

But then, the viral internet stepped in. Last week, a video surfaced showing a Waymo trying to pass two police cars who were trying to slow down traffic on I-280 in Northern California. This is one of the main routes through Silicon Valley, and the opening of highway operations drastically reduced ride times in the area.

The video shows two police cars behind a construction vehicle, lights on and spread out across the freeway. Then it pans to show a Waymo vehicle moving quickly in the far left lane. One of the officers accelerates and swerves in front of the Waymo vehicle, at which point the Waymo swerves and slows down. (One media citation states that the video seems to have been sped up by the original poster, but we’ve embedded the short local news report on it above).

According to recent reports, in response to this, the California DMV contacted Waymo and ordered the manufacturer to pause highway operations while it examines the incident. The order was made on November 11, but wasn’t reported until today.

Recent findings suggest that the DMV cited multiple instances of Waymo vehicles incurring into construction zones, not simply the one viral clip above. It said that previous incidents had occurred and been noted, and corrective actions were implemented, but that the incidents keep happening.

This is a very rare situation which Waymo handled poorly. Waymo will add this case to their their test suite. They'll probably ask the CHP for their in car videos of other cases and convert those to be additional test cases. Waymo has been very willing to admit when their vehicles make mistakes in rare situations and fix it so that it doesn't happen again.

According to recent reports, waymo's vehicles are compared against perfect driving and Waymo accepts that as an aspirational goal. I note Tesla lacks the confidence in their system to even apply for the California permit to begin autonomous testing.

DMV’s pause will remain until Waymo can demonstrate “effective corrective actions” have been taken.

Recent findings suggest that while the DMV’s order only applies to California highways, Waymo also paused highway operations in other states. It remains operating on city streets in all coverage areas.

Update: Waymo emailed us this statement after it saw this article.

According to recent reports, “Safety is at the foundation of everything we do. Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When it comes to body recomposition, showing up and crushing your workouts is only half the equation. You also need to pay attention to your nutrition to build muscle and lose fat.

It has been revealed that and that part of the job isn’t always as straightforward as exercise. In the gym, you know you need to regularly lift enough to challenge your muscles and get your cardio in. In the kitchen, body recomposition typically involves two key things: getting enough protein and managing your calorie intake. As simple as that sounds, it isn’t always easy.

There are a few ways to approach these goals, but one key to making them more sustainable and manageable (and therefore easier to stick to!) is to track your macronutrients, or macros. The three macronutrients are carbohydrates, fats, and protein, and each plays a unique role in your body recomposition journey.

According to recent reports, carbs get a lot of unnecessary hate, but they’re your body’s primary energy source, says Dana White, RD. Your body relies on glucose, a sugar that is broken down from carbs. Without enough of it, your energy, concentration, and mood can all be affected.

Fats are vital to your body’s overall functioning. They support the health of your cells, help your body absorb vitamins like A, D, E, and K, and play a major role in satiety, White notes. Protein, perhaps the most obvious of the three, plays a major role in muscle repair and development—important at any time, but especially on a body recomp journey.

Sources indicate that counting your macros can help you stay on track with your body recomposition journey. To find out how much of each macro you need and how to fill your plate, try our Eating for Body Recomp Guide.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It’s been two years since Lego and Formula 1 first partnered up to translate the excitement of the grand prix grid into tiny, plastic, painful-to-step-on brick form. But while the race cars were a realistic low-polygon tribute to the life-size real things, the minifigures that accompanied them were fairly generic. Until now, that is, because the upcoming Lego Speed Champions lineup features all 11 teams on the 2026 grid and all 22 full-time drivers, rendered with realistic driving suits and customized hair.

Unveiled at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix against a backdrop of several giant minifigures and a full complement of Lego-clad go-karts (now updated with neon LED light strips for the full Vegas experience), this next batch of Speed Champions sets will go on sale March 1, 2027. That makes for plenty of time to build all 11 before the first race of the season in Bahrain, although it’s also yet another thing to wait for during the off-season.

Sources indicate that arvid Lindblad, driver for the Visa Cash App Racing Bulls Team, made at appearance at Lego’s press announcement, and posed with both his large and small Lego likenesses. Asked about his thoughts on the result, the British driver said: “Awesome, nailed it. They got the hair perfect,” adding that, “I’ve always loved Lego, though I never imagined having my own minifigure.” [Brits refer to Lego as a collective singular, like sheep.].

And speaking of hair, yes, the Valteri Bottas minifigure is rocking a mullet. Each plastic hairpiece was approved by the respective drivers. “When we pitched the the hairstyles to the teams and the drivers, they absolutely loved it,” said Will Thorogood, the Lego designer who led this effort. “They all thought it was as funny as we did.”.

Recent findings suggest that another key part of bringing out the driver’s personality is the helmets, which are “far more detailed than any helmet we've ever done before with the with the Lego production,” according to Thorogood. Lando Norris’s helmet, for example, “has all the blob details on it” as well as a minifigure Easter egg hidden in the design. Each driver also comes with two facial expressions on opposite sides of the minfigure head; Charles Leclerc’s visage is either relaxed in sunglasses or a more serious grimace, both with the Ferrari driver’s stubbled mustache and goatee.

The cars themselves reflect the fresh regulations and, says Thorogood, “as you look closely, you'll see every single one is built completely differently to capture all the aero details and principles that each of the teams has employed.” These too feature several Easter eggs for Lego fans, such as suspension wishbones made from wizard wands and rear diffuser strakes made from minifigure meat cleavers.

Measuring 7.5 inches long and 2.5 inches wide, the Speed Champions sets will be priced at $29.99 when they go on sale next year, but you can preorder yours below.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, even Alaska’s bears are not immune from accidentally making things weird or getting a bit too close. Over the summer, rangers at Tongass National Forest in southeastern Alaska watched an odd interaction between two unnamed black bears (Ursus americanus) taking part in Anan Creek’s salmon run.

“Sometimes the bears at Anan share the creek… a little too closely,” the rangers write. “One bear is waiting his turn for a prime fishing spot, and the other is so focused on the fish he doesn’t mind his surroundings. Did the 1st bear make it weird by backing up, or did the 2nd bear make it weird by staying there?”.

For this bit of humor, the rangers awarded the unnamed bears with the 2026 You Made it Weird Award.

Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the Anan Bear Awards to the 39 bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska over the summer.

Sources indicate that the largest national forest in the United States, Tongass covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles, and plenty of bears on the hunt for food. One of the hotspots is Anan Creek, home to one of the largest runs of pink salmon in the region. As such, the creek is a very popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their chunky counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast on salmon and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And also like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear here has their own habits and quirks.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their antics.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Hyundai revealed the production-ready Neira EV for the first time, a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV set to launch in Indonesia on November 20.

After introducing the Neira Concept at the 2026 Gaikindo Indonesia International Auto Show (GIIAS) in July, Hyundai is gearing up to open pre-orders on November 20.

The Neira is a pretty “big” deal as Hyundai’s first locally produced seven-seat electric SUV in Indonesia.

Ahead of its official debut on Friday at GAIKINDO Auto Week (GAW) 2026, Hyundai offered a closer look at the upcoming Neira.

The electric SUV is essentially a Hyundai-badged version of the Kia Carens Clavis EV that launched last year. Aside from the Hyundai logos, a few minor tweaks to the front and rear ends, and new wheels and headlights, it’s a near replica.

Inside, both are equipped with dual 12.3″ instrument display and center navigation screens, plus an added climate control panel.

Hyundai didn’t reveal battery or powertrain specs, but the Neira is expected to use the same 42 kWh and 51.4 kWh battery packs as the Carens Clavis EV. The former offers an MIDC range of up to 251 mi (404 km), while the latter has up to 304 mi (490 km) on a single charge.

Both batteries can be charged from 10% to 80% in around 39 minutes using a 100 kW DC fast charger.

The Kia Carens Clavis is 4,550 mm long, 1,800 mm wide, and 1,708 mm tall, with a 2,780 mm wheelbase, so Hyundai’s Neira will likely be about the same size, if not slightly bigger.

Hyundai said the Neira has four key advantages: A higher ground clearance, Hyundai Bluelink connectivity tech, a Blind-spot View Monitor (BVM), and easy third-row access.

A post shared by Hyundai Motors Indonesia (@hyundaimotorindonesia).

Ahead of its upcoming launch, Hyundai is taking the electric 7-seater on a trip to prove its capabilities, going from Kilometer Nol in Banda Aceh to Banda Neira, which is about 4,000 kilometers (about 2,500 miles).

While Hyundai may export the Neira EV to overseas markets like India, don’t expect it to reach the US.

Hyundai already sells a three-row, seven-seat electric SUV, the IONIQ 9, which is built at Hyundai’s Metaplant in Georgia.

#189954. Thanksgiving Outside the Echo Chamber

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (953 w)

Thanksgiving Outside the Echo Chamber

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (953 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Updated November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Gary Drevitch.
  • “Polarized” has been one of the most overused words to describe America's political climate, but it is increasingly being applied to school boards, neighborhoods, and even families as well.
  • Historically, the weird uncle at the Thanksgiving table could be counted on to tell a few off-color jokes or ask a child to pull his finger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Updated November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Gary Drevitch.

“Polarized” has been one of the most overused words to describe America's political climate, but it is increasingly being applied to school boards, neighborhoods, and even families as well. Affective polarization, or the growing dislike and distrust of people on the opposing side of the political aisle, has more than doubled in the U.S. since the late 1970s (Boxell et al., 2024). Many of us now surround ourselves with like-minded friends and partners, creating a world in which we watch news, follow influencers, and make friends with people who reinforce what we already believe. This all gets thrown out the window at Thanksgiving, when we leave the safety of our echo chamber and spend time with the family we didn’t choose but love anyway.

Historically, the weird uncle at the Thanksgiving table could be counted on to tell a few off-color jokes or ask a child to pull his finger. These offenses seem almost quaint now that a passing comment about politics or social justice can leave half the table questioning the moral character of the other half. This annual exercise ends in one of two ways: The dinner crescendos into an actual altercation with one side accusing the other of crimes against humanity, or everyone smiles politely, and then unloads their thoughts and feelings to their significant other on the ride home. I’d like to propose a third option: intellectual curiosity.

What if we approached a conversation with someone whose political beliefs we find baffling with a genuine interest in how they came to hold those beliefs in the first place? It is true that not all beliefs are equal (beliefs such as racial superiority are indefensible); however, many people come to believe something they consider logical based on their life experience. For example: free college for all. Imagine cutting into the turkey when one family member casually says free college could open doors for students whose families can’t afford an education, and another relative pipes up that that wouldn’t be fair. Eating slows, as everyone recognizes dinner just got awkward.

Rather than writing off the relative you disagree with, use this time to practice intellectual curiosity, or the desire to learn, explore new ideas, and better understand something, even when it challenges what we already believe. This requires a couple of steps. The first is to pause. Polarizing comments are often triggering, and people often get angry before anything else. Recognize the anger and then pause until the initial rush passes.

Next, commit to intellectual curiosity by asking instead of telling. In the free college example, this may mean replying with, “I’d like to hear more about that. What feels unfair to you?” And then sit back and actually listen. Make eye contact, don’t interrupt, and don’t prepare your next argument. Doing this requires the next step: using your Theory of Mind.

Theory of Mind is the ability to understand that others have thoughts, beliefs, desires, and intentions that differ from our own. Because we can’t open someone’s head and look inside, we don’t know what they're actually thinking, but we gather clues from what they say and how they act to develop a theory of their mind. Theory of Mind develops rapidly across childhood and adolescence and continues into adulthood. This doesn’t mean all adults are good at it; in fact, I’d argue that most aren’t. We're already using Theory of Mind when we judge our relatives. We're just doing it with very little information and potentially a great deal of bias. When someone opposes free college, we might immediately assume they're selfish or indifferent to disadvantaged students. That assumption is itself a theory of their mind. Asking questions allows us to gather better information and revise that theory. At the Thanksgiving table, this means trying to put yourself in their shoes and take their perspective.

Recent findings suggest that finally, we can muster empathy. We’ve asked questions, revised our theory of their mind (why they believe what they do), and we still disagree with them. That’s okay; we can hold our beliefs and still find space in our heart to empathize with theirs. To return to the free college debate, imagine that a relative shares that they had to graduate in 5 years rather than 4 because they worked two jobs to pay for their education. Despite this, it still took them 17 years and a lot of low-budget vacations to pay off their loans, a milestone they just recently celebrated. Suddenly the word “fair” hits differently. You empathize with their situation, although you may still retain your initial position.

It has been revealed that by the end of the night, you may still find your uncle’s political beliefs baffling, but you’ll better understand how he came to hold them. Given how much time we spend speculating about the minds of people we disagree with, why not take advantage of having one sitting across the table from us? Ask a few questions, entertain the possibility that you’ve misjudged someone, and see where the conversation goes. You might even have a more pleasant ride home.

Sources indicate that boxell, L., Gentzkow, M., & Shapiro, J. M. (2024). Cross-country trends in affective polarization. The Review of Economics and Statistics, 106(2), 557–565. doi.org/10.1162/rest_a_01160.

Premack, D., & Woodruff, G. (1978). Does the chimpanzee have a theory of mind? Behavioral and Brain Sciences, 1(4), 515–526. doi.org/10.1017/S0140525X00076512.

Stanley, M. L., Sinclair, A. H., & Seli, P. (2020). Intellectual humility and perceptions of political opponents. Journal of Personality, 88(6), 1196–1216. doi.org/10.1111/jopy.12566.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that hospital ratings have become an key resource for choosing where to receive care. They influence which doctors patients choose, how far they are willing to travel, and whether they seek care at a different facility.

On October 27, Healthgrades unveiled the recipients of the 2027 Specialty Excellence Outpatient Awards and Specialty State Rankings.

In a recent development, the annual awards recognize hospitals delivering outstanding patient outcomes in specialty care across the United States. Healthgrades is the leading platform used by Americans for finding a doctor or hospital.

New research from Healthgrades highlights that hospital quality is increasingly a factor in healthcare decisions.

In a recent development, around 80% of patients report that when looking for a doctor, the quality of the hospital where they practice matters. Additionally, 7 in 10 patients (68%) say they’re more likely to seek care for a procedure or health condition from a doctor who works at a hospital with high quality ratings.

What’s more, around 71% of patients say they would switch doctors to gain access to a higher-rated hospital.

“Our specialty awards identify the nation’s top-performing hospitals across numerous medical specialties, helping consumers find high quality care tailored to their specific needs,” stated Alana Biggers, MD, MPH, medical advisor at Healthgrades.

Industry observers note that healthgrades is owned by RVO Health. By clicking on this link, we may receive a commission. Learn more.

“Navigating the complex healthcare system can feel daunting, but taking a proactive stance to understand where to access superior care can enhance your healthcare journey and overall experience. The ability to make informed decisions about your health — and where to get care — is a cornerstone of self-advocacy, and we are proud to help make that information accessible to all patients.”.

Healthgrades identifies hospitals that deliver exceptional outcomes across common outpatient procedures and specialty conditions.

Finding high quality care is notable, particularly amid a growing gap between top-performing and one-star hospitals.

According to Healthgrades, from 2023 to 2025, if all hospitals had performed at the five-star level from 2023 to 2025:.

“One of the biggest challenges is balancing increasing patient needs with the resources available to healthcare professionals,” Biggers said.

Industry observers note that “Hospitals face workforce shortages, growing administrative responsibilities, financial pressures, and increasing complexity in patient care. Physicians and other healthcare professionals need adequate time and support not only to evaluate and treat patients, but also to communicate results, coordinate follow-up care, and address concerns that arise between visits,” she continued.

“When healthcare teams are adequately supported, they are better positioned to communicate effectively with patients, coordinate care, and address patients’ needs.”.

Biggers said that ensuring equal access to quality healthcare is challenging because of factors such as:.

Sources indicate that hospital closures and reduced services make access even more difficult. Biggers identified a few possible solutions, such as expanding outpatient care, building community partnerships, using telehealth when appropriate, and improving coordination among healthcare providers.

Sources indicate that “Ultimately, providing high quality care requires more than clinical expertise. It requires healthcare systems to invest in their workforce, strengthen care coordination, and create environments where healthcare professionals have the resources they need to provide safe, effective, and patient-centered care,” Biggers remarked.

“Equally vital, healthcare systems must ensure that patients have meaningful access to these services, regardless of where they live or their socioeconomic circumstances.”.

Healthgrades acknowledges hospitals that excel in three aspects of specialty care:.

Biggers mentioned that outstanding hospitals recognize that high quality care extends beyond just treating an illness.

“It involves listening to patients, understanding their individual circumstances, and ensuring they feel respected, informed, and involved in their healthcare decisions,” she said.

Patients want to find a hospital that excels in the procedures or health conditions relevant to them.

The recipients of the Specialty Excellence Awards are among the top 15% of hospitals specializing in these areas.

Healthgrades evaluated patient outcomes at roughly 4,500 hospitals across 31 common procedures and conditions to reach their decisions.

Among the list of Specialty Excellence Award recipients, Healthgrades also recognizes America’s 100 Best Hospitals for Specialty Care for 11 specialty areas andAmerica’s 50 Best Hospitals for Specialty Care for four specialty areas.

“An outstanding hospital prioritizes both patient care and the people delivering that care,” Biggers told Healthline.

“While clinical outcomes, patient safety, and access to evidence-based treatments are essential measures of quality, I believe hospitals must also invest in workforce development and support. This means ensuring physicians, nurses, and other healthcare professionals have appropriate staffing levels, adequate clinical and administrative support, and opportunities for continued professional development,” she continued.

Healthgrades awards U.S. hospitals that excel at Outpatient Orthopedic Surgery, Outpatient Joint Replacement, andOutpatient Prostate Care.

Outpatient care is one of the fastest-growing areas of healthcare. The number of orthopedic procedures performed in an outpatient environment has grown exponentially in recent years.

In a recent development, from 2020 to 2025, outpatient hip replacement procedures grew by 81%, while inpatient procedures dropped by 75%. Outpatient knee replacements increased by 71% while inpatient volumes decreased by 70%.

“I believe several factors are contributing to the growing demand for outpatient care, including advances in medical technology, a greater emphasis on preventive care, and the increasing need to manage chronic medical conditions,” Biggers said.

Sources indicate that “Many services and procedures that previously required hospitalization can now be safely performed in outpatient settings. Patients also appreciate the convenience of receiving care closer to home and avoiding unnecessary hospital stays,” she added.

To meet the increasing demand for outpatient procedures, Biggers cautioned that healthcare systems must ensure that these services are adequately staffed and supported.

“Effective communication and coordination between outpatient providers, specialists, and hospitals are essential to maintaining continuity and quality of care,” she said.

State Rankings identify the top three or five hospitals in eligible states across 19 key specialty areas.

The rankings are based on clinical performance and build on the 2027 Healthgrades Specialty Excellence Awards Methodology.

State-level specialty care rankings help consumers find outstanding local hospitals for their condition or procedure.

The analysis used Medicare inpatient data from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) from 2023 to 2025, and assessed patient outcomes across 31 conditions and procedures.

These outcomes served as the foundation for determining Specialty Excellence Awards and state hospital rankings.

With consumer-facing awards and ratings influencing healthcare decisions, transparency about their methods and limitations remains essential.

Ratings can help patients ask better questions and compare options, but they should complement — not replace — clinical guidance and informed decision making.

Iceland’s first wind farm comes with a water-saving bonus

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1327 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.
  • Vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads.
  • Industry observers note that landsvirkjun, Iceland’s national power company, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later.

Vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads. And Iceland’s windiest months coincide with the time of year when less water flows into its reservoirs.

Industry observers note that landsvirkjun, Iceland’s national power company, officially commissioned Vaðölduver on September 15, 2026. The first 14 turbines are online; another 14 will be installed in a second phase, and the entire wind farm is expected to be operating by the end of 2027.

It has been revealed that once complete, Vaðölduver will have 120 megawatts (MW) of capacity. When I met with the folks at Landsvirkjun in Reykjavik last month, they told me that’s enough to power the equivalent of 90,000 Icelandic households. Vaðalda’s electricity feeds into the grid and is sold through power purchase agreements.

Vaðölduver sits on a lava-and-sand plain east of the Þjórsá River, south of Sultartangi Dam. Landsvirkjun already operates seven hydropower stations in the surrounding Þjórsá and Tungnaá region.

The wind farm was sited in this region of Iceland because the seasons line up nicely.

Recent findings suggest that the winds are strongest in winter, when inflows into hydropower reservoirs can be low. In summer, wind speeds tend to drop, but glacial melt increases water availability for the hydropower system.

Recent findings suggest that when the wind turbines are generating plenty of electricity, Landsvirkjun can ease off hydropower and leave more water in its reservoirs. When the wind drops, hydropower can pick up more of the demand.

That gives the utility more control over when it uses its stored water and helps that water go further.

Industry observers note that german wind turbine maker Enercon manufactured Vaðölduver’s turbines. The project also includes a service and maintenance agreement with Enercon.

Landsvirkjun had a decade of experience operating pilot wind turbines before building Vaðölduver. One big thing they learned: They didn’t need tall towers to find plenty of wind.

In a recent development, there’s little vegetation or other surface obstructions across this unique, exposed landscape. That allows the turbines to capture productive winds closer to the ground than they could at a more wooded or sheltered location.

“Lower” is relative, of course. The turbines still reach 150 meters (492 feet) at their highest blade tip.

Recent findings suggest that the wind farm covers 17.1 square kilometers (6.6 square miles). Twenty-five turbines are rated at 4.26 MW each, and the remaining three at 4.5 MW. Landsvirkjun’s presentation puts annual generation at 440 GWh and lists a P50 net efficiency figure of 43%, which is considered strong for onshore wind.

It has been revealed that the ability to tap into existing infrastructure was a major factor in Landsvirkjun’s site selection. Where a wind farm goes affects its cost, its environmental footprint, and the people who live nearby.

In a recent development, landsvirkjun also identifies active engagement with communities and other stakeholders as essential to building wind projects. At Vaðölduver, the immediate task is to finish the remaining 14 turbines while the first phase completes its trial runs.

Recent findings suggest that the company sees wind as a potential third pillar of Iceland’s electricity supply alongside hydropower and geothermal. Vaðölduver shows how those resources can work together, with wind adding generation while helping conserve stored water.

According to recent reports, iceland is a world leader in clean energy. It generates nearly 100% of its electricity from renewable sources, combining hydropower fueled by glacial runoff and rivers (around 70%) and geothermal energy (around 30%).

Over 90% of Icelandic households use direct geothermal hot water for space heating and hot water, while the remaining homes use renewable electricity.

In a recent development, but it’s got the same grid capacity challenges as every other country. Adding wind – and anything else that uses power – means paying close attention to what the grid can handle. Iceland has an isolated transmission system, so maintaining stability and ensuring sufficient capacity are increasingly important as the country develops more projects.

Recent findings suggest that while in Reykjavik, I met with the Minister of the Environment, Energy and Climate, Jóhann Páll Jóhannsson, who told me that the Icelandic grid’s capacity is expected to grow from 20 TWh to 24-25 TWh within a decade. Jóhannsson also stated that he is pro-data center and that investors are keen to establish more of them in the country.

When I asked Jóhannsson and his team, as well as the teams at Landsvirkjun and publicly owned ON Power, Iceland’s second-largest electricity generator and largest EV charger network, about grid expansion intends to handle that pipeline, they all remarked that legislative reforms were being passed to speed up energy permitting processes. There is also financing in place to grow the grid. The physical transmission network is being expanded, but the process is slow because NIMBYism is creating bottlenecks.

In learning about new and completed Icelandic power projects during my visit, it was apparent that the companies in the power and geothermal heat sector regularly collaborate on projects – everyone brings their expertise to the table and works for the common good (yes, really).

Sources indicate that but what was striking in discussions about grid expansion was that there seemed to be no prepares to pitch in with the Icelandic transmission system operator (TSO), Landsnet hf. It seemed that the proposal was to let the TSO come up with the solutions on its own. At most, Jóhannsson’s team noted its legislative reform “opened the door” to possible grid innovations.

When I asked the Landsvirkjun team whether they were considering working with the TSO on distributed energy resource (DER) projects like virtual power plants and onsite battery storage for its heavy-industry clients, which make up 80% of its business, they said they hadn’t considered it.

Sources indicate that I often wonder why Quebec hasn't followed this strategy. They have huge dams with world-leading power connections, and one of the glitch they are facing is a lack of water to refill those dams, due to several years of relative drought. I know it costs a lot to build wind power up north, but siting a project there would re-use their massive investment in power lines. The dams would act as gigantic batteries, because they wouldn't need to drain their reservoirs when the wind is blowing.

Iceland has earned its reputation as a clean energy leader. Bringing that same collaborative and creative approach to expanding its grid would help it keep setting an example for the rest of the world.

Hackers use old Bitly links to re-direct to offensive content

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (528 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Be wary of the next few shortened website links you click on social media.
  • That’s a polite way of putting it, since many of the hijacked URLs sent unsuspecting people on detours to inappropriate, obscene, and offensive webpages ranging from Wikipedia entries on the Holocaust and 9/11, to vulgar YouTube audio clips.
  • According to recent reports, link-shortening is one of the internet’s simplest and most convenient workarounds.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Be wary of the next few shortened website links you click on social media. According to the service provider Bitly, its hyperlinks in older tweets from many companies, politicians, and even government accounts are now redirecting to “content unrelated to the original posts.”.

That’s a polite way of putting it, since many of the hijacked URLs sent unsuspecting people on detours to inappropriate, obscene, and offensive webpages ranging from Wikipedia entries on the Holocaust and 9/11, to vulgar YouTube audio clips.

According to recent reports, link-shortening is one of the internet’s simplest and most convenient workarounds. The service typically works by pinning a website’s lengthy, complex URL address to a tidied-up, abbreviated shortcut in a digital registry. This shortened address then redirects anyone who clicks it to their intended online destination.

Well…in theory. Security analysts have tried to warn people about an issue known as “bit rot” for decades. In 2009—about one year after Bitly’s debut—Silicon Valley entrepreneur Joshua Schacter wrote a prescient blog post cautioning against what he felt were potentially serious flaws in the link-shortening “middleman” system. Amid the concerns, Schacter cited a “fresh and potentially unreliable” tool that ties an original hyperlink to the “health of a third party.”.

“The shortener may decide a link is a Terms Of Service violation and delete it. If the shortener accidentally erases a database, forgets to renew its domain, or just disappears, the link will break,” he explained. “If a top-level domain changes its policy on commercial use, the link will break. If the shortener gets hacked, every link becomes a potential phishing attack.”.

It now appears bad actors recently identified countless of these Bitly links previously posted across social media between 2009 and 2014. Although their exact methods aren’t clear, it’s possible they generated their own custom Bitly links using the addresses in the social media posts, then used those to send people to different destinations. Bitly claims its links do not automatically expire, but paid owners may redirect existing links.

Many examples were found among the more than 60,000 posts on X from President Donald Trump’s official account. In one of Trump’s previous posts about his golf course in Scotland, the Bitly link temporarily redirected to Wikipedia’s entry on the Epstein Files. Targets also included corporations like McDonald’s, with one of the fast food giant’s 2011 Bitly URLs suddenly linked to Wikipedia’s page about the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

It has been revealed that not every hijacked post funneled people to upsetting outcomes. Instead of a cybersecurity PSA, the Bitly address in a 2021 post from the FBI briefly linked to a photo of a blubbery seal. Another of Trump’s URLs sent you to the popular video game, Geometry Dash.

In its acknowledgement of the problem on November 15, Bitly reported it had identified and suspended the bad actors’ accounts, and were in the process of “disabling the affected links.”.

“Our Trust and Safety team is working to address the matter and strengthen protections against similar misuse in the future,” Bitly wrote at the time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Old solar panels have silver and copper worth recovering. A latest US recycling organization called Jupiter prepares to send metals recovered from retired solar panels and data center hardware to Korea Zinc’s refineries, including a $7.4 billion plant planned for Clarksville, Tennessee.

Jupiter joins US solar panel recycler Solarcycle and PedalPoint Recycling, Korea Zinc’s US recycling and metals business, into a single, fully integrated tech giant. Jupiter says it’s launching with eight certified US facilities, nearly 1 million square feet of processing space, and about 250 employees. It’s also taking on customers from both businesses, including Microsoft, Prologis, and Brookfield.

Sources indicate that for a solar farm or data center operator, that means a single tech giant can take equipment out of service, resell parts with remaining useful life, and recycle the rest. Customers can track where the materials go and bring them back into their own supply chains.

Korea Zinc will hold a majority stake. Solarcycle’s Suvi Sharma will lead Jupiter as CEO, and PedalPoint’s Kevin Hahm will be CFO. Microsoft and Prologis Ventures are among Solarcycle’s existing investors.

As Electrek reported in January, Solarcycle’s Cedartown, Georgia, plant was processing thousands of old solar panels a week when it opened. Solarcycle said the plant could handle up to 5 gigawatts’ worth of panels annually at full capacity, recovering materials such as glass, aluminum, copper, and silver.

The Tennessee plant adds a US refining step. Korea Zinc is developing the facility, called Project Crucible, with US government backing. It expects to start production in phases in 2029. The plant is designed to process about 1.1 million tons of raw materials per year and produce roughly 540,000 tons of finished products.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • On November 17, the nonprofit advocacy group Survival International reported a recent incident in which 20 members of the Awá people intentionally contacted local government officials in the Brazilian Amazon.
  • “This is a troubling indication of how the continued invasion of uncontacted peoples’ forests puts otherwise self-sufficient Indigenous people in real danger,” Survival International director Caroline Pearce noted in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Around the world, the number of uncontacted Indigenous tribes continues to dwindle. Indigenous rights advocates estimate that half of the nearly 200 communities still existing in comparative isolation could disappear within a decade, without proper safeguards against climate change, land loss, fame-seeking opportunists, and illegal industrial encroachments. Unfortunately, the situation has apparently grown so dire that some Indigenous groups are reaching out for help—and exposing themselves to potentially deadly foreign diseases in the process.

On November 17, the nonprofit advocacy group Survival International reported a recent incident in which 20 members of the Awá people intentionally contacted local government officials in the Brazilian Amazon. Although proficient hunter-gatherers, the group requested yams before taking them back into the rainforest.

“This is a troubling indication of how the continued invasion of uncontacted peoples’ forests puts otherwise self-sufficient Indigenous people in real danger,” Survival International director Caroline Pearce noted in a statement.

Sources indicate that the Awá are one of the world’s last uncontacted Indigenous tribes, whose ties to the Brazilian rainforest stretch back centuries. They faced their first attacks from European settlers during the 1800s, which eventually forced them to adopt a nomadic lifestyle to avoid future encounters. Brazil finally supplied the Awá with settlement areas during the mid-1980s, but it still took years before the government properly invested in demarcated land. In the meantime, numerous deadly interactions with loggers, farmers, and other illegal intruders had reduced the Awá community to barely 300 people. Of those, advocates estimate only about one-third of the hunter-gatherers remain completely isolated from the outside world.

“The Brazilian government must commit the resources necessary to protect [the region of] Arariboia from the loggers and ranchers who are razing it, in flagrant defiance of the law,” Pearce added.

In addition to the advocacy work by Survival International, the Awá are supported by a team of Indigenous members of the Guajajara community known as the Forest Guardians. These volunteers have spent years pushing back against illegal cattle ranchers and loggers attempting to claim land in Arariboia, often dying as a result of their efforts.

Recent findings suggest that “The Forest Guardians have always worked to protect the Awá against encroachment, even at the cost of losing warriors in battle,” the organization said. “We demand immediate action from the relevant authorities…to ensure what the Awá believe is best for them, safeguarding their lives, health, safety and dignity. FOR THE AWÁ, FOR THE TENETEHAR [language], AND FOR THE FOREST!”.

Latest Update: 6 to 8 Cups of Tea Daily May Reduce Heart Disease Risk by 11%

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (624 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that people who regularly drink tea may have an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease, which includes conditions such as stroke, heart disease, and peripheral artery disease.
  • Both black tea and green tea may offer heart health benefits.
  • The lowest overall vascular risk was seen among tea drinkers who were also physically active and didn’t smoke.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that people who regularly drink tea may have an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease, which includes conditions such as stroke, heart disease, and peripheral artery disease. This is according to a study published on October 21 in the Journal of Internal Medicine.

Both black tea and green tea may offer heart health benefits. However, the study shows an association rather than proving that drinking tea prevents cardiovascular disease.

The lowest overall vascular risk was seen among tea drinkers who were also physically active and didn’t smoke.

The study followed 485,934 people ages 30–79 from the China Kadoorie Biobank for an average of 9 years.

The researchers found that regular tea drinkers had an 11% lower overall risk of vascular disease compared with those who did not regularly drink tea. They also observed a 37% lower risk of ischemic stroke and a 17% lower risk of heart attack.

There was no clear link for hemorrhagic stroke or pulmonary heart disease.

Recent findings suggest that among people who drank tea at least weekly, the lowest estimated risk was seen in those consuming approximately 6–8 cups per day. However, the findings do not establish this as a recommended daily intake.

Amit Blumfield, MD, a cardiologist with Manhattan Cardiology in NYC who wasn’t involved in the study, told Healthline that it is important to remember this is observational data.

Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) examining the effects of drinking black and green tea on lipids and blood pressure showed only modest, non-significant benefits.

The study also had limitations, including self-reported tea consumption and the possibility that other dietary and lifestyle factors influenced the results.

“Overall, tea seems to, maybe, have some cardiovascular benefits without a significant risk, so I favor tea consumption,” he said.

Michelle Routhenstein, a preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished who was not involved in the research, emphasized that the findings do not establish a cause-and-effect relationship between drinking tea and a lower risk of vascular disease.

“Tea can be a helpful addition to a heart-healthy lifestyle, but it is not a substitute for addressing individual cardiovascular risk factors,” she said.

The researchers also found that drinking “burning hot” tea increased the risk of vascular disease by 16%, consistent with previous research raising concerns about the consumption of very hot beverages.

“I recommend enjoying your tea’s potential benefits by letting it cool to a comfortable sipping temperature before you drink it,” stated Routhenstein.

The study examined black, green, Oolong, and other tea types.

It has been revealed that the researchers found that black tea indicated a more consistent association with a lower risk of vascular disease, which is contrary to some earlier research. However, they noted that these results don’t establish black tea as superior to green tea, and they don’t mean you should switch tea types.

“Both black and green tea are great choices for your heart health, and neither is definitively better than the other,” stated Routhenstein.

“I recommend choosing whichever you enjoy and consuming it consistently, ideally without much added sugar,” Routhenstein noted.

Blumfield also noted that adding sugar or non-sugar sweeteners may change the potential health effects of drinking tea, so the findings should not automatically be extended to sweetened tea beverages.

Some older research suggests there may be additional health benefits to drinking both black and green tea. These benefits may include:.

Routhenstein said that tea may also support focus and alertness, improve hydration status, and potentially play a role in metabolic health.

“Enjoying tea can be a simple way to incorporate beneficial plant compounds into your day,” she added.

While drinking tea has been considered a health-promoting habit since ancient times, more research is needed to confirm its various health benefits.

Tens of millions of crabs are crossing Christmas Island. Here’s how to watch.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Christmas Island red crabs (Gecarcoidea natalis) have officially begun their annual migration on the tiny Australian territory in the Indian Ocean.
  • The migration begins with the first rainfall of the wet season, typically in October or November, but can be as late as December or January.
  • Industry observers note that according to Christmas Island National Park, the speed and timing of the migration is determined by the moon’s phases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The crabs are coming. Millions upon millions of them. Christmas Island red crabs (Gecarcoidea natalis) have officially begun their annual migration on the tiny Australian territory in the Indian Ocean.

The migration begins with the first rainfall of the wet season, typically in October or November, but can be as late as December or January. Red crabs from all over Christmas Island will leave their homes in the forest at the same time and start their march towards the ocean. Once they reach the ocean, they will mate and spawn. The male crabs lead the migration, while the females join in along the way.

Industry observers note that according to Christmas Island National Park, the speed and timing of the migration is determined by the moon’s phases. “Red crabs always spawn before dawn on a receding high-tide during the last quarter of the moon,” the park rangers write. “Incredibly, they know exactly when to leave their burrows to make this lunar date.”.

It has been revealed that however, the crabs will wait until the first rainfall to begin their journey, so they sometimes have to hurry. If the rains arrive close to their optimal spawning date, the crabs will move to the ocean very rapidly. If the rain comes early, the crustaceans may take their time, “stopping to eat and drink on their way to the coast.” If rain begins too late to make the spawning date, some of the crabs will remain in their burrows and begin their migration the following month.

The result is spectacular. Tens of millions of bright red crustaceans the size of a soda can spread out over the 12-mile-wide island on their way to the ocean. They begin their march inland and will reach their destination in about nine days. In 2008, naturalist and documentarian Sir David Attenborough described the annual event as one of his best television moments.

Over the next few days Parks Australia will run livestreams of the migration for about 60 minutes. The exact timing and number of livestreams can’t be scheduled in advance since it is completely dependent on the crabs.

“We will aim to livestream in the morning, but the crabs will have the final say on when and how many days they will venture across the bridge,” the rangers write.

Filming occurs at the red crab bridge, a 16-foot-tall structure built to help the crabs cross the busy road. The crabs will migrate past this bridge for about three to four days.

#189943. Breaking: Why Stress Is Good for You

Breaking: Why Stress Is Good for You

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1358 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Michelle Quirk.
  • The old story about stress is that you wanted to avoid it wherever possible, and you especially wanted to avoid responding to stressors if you could.
  • This old story has been found to be absurdly, wildly wrong, but still it persists like a bad dream, while those of us who respond powerfully to life's ups and downs have been taught to question ourselves constantly (and then stress out about our stress responses).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 24, 2026 | Reviewed by Michelle Quirk.

The old story about stress is that you wanted to avoid it wherever possible, and you especially wanted to avoid responding to stressors if you could. You wanted to be calm, untroubled, and chill most of the time.

This old story has been found to be absurdly, wildly wrong, but still it persists like a bad dream, while those of us who respond powerfully to life's ups and downs have been taught to question ourselves constantly (and then stress out about our stress responses).

The fresh story may surprise you, because it focuses on the strengthening power of stressors, the health benefits of a strong stress response, and the cognitive interventions that can help you access the healing heart of stress.

First things first. Stress is not a thing that happens to you; it's a deeply individual response to something that matters to you.

It has been revealed that an alternative definition for the word stress is to underscore, highlight, or focus on something because it's crucial to you. Your stress responses are connected to how much importance you place on a potential stressor. The higher your stress response, the more importance the stressor has for you.

Sources indicate that if your stress response is high, you're not failing at being chill, and the stressor didn't make you react; you're marking something as deeply notable and worthy of your focus and attention. So the first intervention is to focus on what's important to you.

In her book The Upside of Stress: Why Stress is Good for You and How to Get Good at It, researcher Kelly McGonigal focuses on a research-backed group of simple mindset interventions that help people reframe their relationship with their stress responses.

Recent findings suggest that instead of trying to get you to calm down, McGonigal helps you identify and then write about the values that are most key to you. This might seem to be a strange approach, but the connection between importance and your stress response is very clear. As such, connecting to your values can help you identify and then learn about the things that mean the most to you.

With these interventions, your stress responses can help you develop deep knowledge about who you are and what's crucial to you. And perhaps, instead of seeing yourself as a stressed-out mess, you can reframe yourself as a person who feels deeply and cares deeply.

If you've been exposed to any form of stress management, mindfulness, or meditation that pathologizes your stress responses, you need to read The Upside of Stress and support yourself with healthier ideas.

In part 2 of this series, I focused on a surprising and heartening aspect of our newer knowledge about stress: The strength of your stress response is not a problem at all, because it's directly connected to your resilience and your skills.

Sources indicate that you may have heard the saying, "Teach your butterflies to fly in formation." This comes from people like actors, athletes, skydivers, and other professionals who choose to be in stressful situations as a part of their livelihoods. Research has shown that high-performing people don't develop lower stress responses over time; they stay high. But what changes over time is their relationship to their stress responses.

It has been revealed that instead of fretting or trying to manage, suppress, or downregulate their stress responses, high-performing people learn to reframe their heightened activation as necessary for preparation and mastery. Many even learn to see their robust stress responses as zest for life.

Sources indicate that this is true even for people like skydivers, whose work (or play) is literally life-endangering. Their stress responses are valuable forms of activation that prepare them for uncertainty (and fun).

It has been revealed that learning to reframe your stress responses means learning how to support your necessary activation as you face uncertainty. Stress is good for you.

In part 1 of this series, I focused on the "weasel word" of stress, which hides the true, emotional nature of our stress responses from us. Unmasking our emotions and learning how to identify and work with the energy and focus they bring to us means that we can develop robust skills for times when the chips are down, and our deepest values are engaged.

According to recent reports, researcher Lisa Feldman Barrett (and colleagues) have shown that simply identifying and naming our emotions with precision can help us develop strong emotion regulation skills—with no other intervention. So, if we persist in misidentifying our emotions with the weasel word of stress, we can't develop those skills.

In part 1, I identified the three powerful emotions that are usually a part of our stress response (anxiety, panic, and anger), and I offered some ideas for how to work with them intentionally. My book, The Language of Emotions, focuses on how we can learn to access the astonishing genius in all of our emotions.

In a recent development, another old story about stress is that our brains react to the world: A stressor "happens," and our brains and bodies react without thought or choice. But researchers have understood for decades that our brains are predicting the future instead of reacting like hapless jack-in-the-boxes.

This predictive nature means that our brains are using our stores of past knowledge to help us make predictions and decisions about what may happen next.

If we believe outdated and damaging information about our stress responses, that bad information will become a self-perpetuating part of our predictions, and we'll misread our activation as a problem instead of a necessary part of preparation, resilience, and mastery.

In a recent development, when we have better information about stress, the values we hold, the importance of our strong stress responses, and the emotional truth hidden inside the weasel word of stress, we can reframe stress as necessary. And we can set ourselves up for better predictions in the future.

💡 Key Takeaways
